text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7142.
ALL PAPERS
- The cabinet is expected to discuss today immigration quotas for 1997, to hear a report on auditing activity and possibly amend a 1975 cabinet decree on implementing the act on social insurance.

- Industry and Trade Minister Szabolcs Fazekas and Turkish State Minister Ayfer Yilmaz signed a free trade agreement in Budapest yesterday, according to which Turkish customs duties will be abolished at a faster rate than those of Hungary.
- A senior Palestinian official said it is possible that Yasser Arafat will visit Budapest in the spring.
- Socialist MP Mihaly Bihari recommended to the executive presidium of the Socialist Parliamentary group that MPs pass the conflict of interest bill again without changes.
- Justice Minister Pal Vastagh said that his ministry must submit 15 bills to Parliament in 1997.

- Christian Democrat President Gyorgy Giczy said his party will appeal Tuesday's Metropolitan Court decision which struck down all decisions passed by the board meeting last December, ruling that the meeting was improperly convened.

- Hungary recorded a balance of payments deficit of $31 million last November, the central bank announced. The more or less continuous decline in last year's deficit is attributed to high tourism revenues and low interest payments.
- The Board of Directors of the State Privatisation and Holding Co. yesterday decided that gas distribution company shares owed to local governments will be distributed without delay.
- Most Hungarian brokers do not think that the unprecedented stock exchange boom of the past few days is excessive. The BUX Index went up almost 100 points in yesterday's trading.

- As nearly 10,000 subscribers wanted to log on to hear Prime Minister Gyula Horn answer questions in a live Internet interview, the system broke down under the load, and the interview appeared on the World Wide Web after a delay of several hours.
- The Army Chief of Staff yesterday dismissed Major Robert Kirschner, who a day earlier opened fire on a photographer at a street crossing in Budapest.
NEPSZABADSAG

- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs told Israel Singer, General Secretary of the World Jewish Congress at an unscheduled meeting during his visit to Israel this week that Hungary's Jewish compensation programme will be completed in February.
VILAGGAZDASAG

- The head of the international law department at the Foreign Ministry said that it is necessary to settle the dispute with Slovakia over the diversion of the Danube in the International Court of Justice in the Hague, as Slovakia will never concede a violation of international law related to the construction of the Gabcikovo hydropower plant.
- The performance of the processing industry declined last month.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- The average annual yield of three-month treasury bills went down at yesterday's auction from 22.08 percent last week to 21.5 percent.

- The German company Bayernwerk and Austria's Energieversorgung Niederosterreich will probably buy shares in regional electricity distribution companies Edasz and Demasz from Electricite de France, reports this paper.
